rationale: The book's core derives 'the life' directly from the supplied OT texts (Deut 30:19-20 choosing life by loving/obeying/cleaving because 'he is thy life'; Lev 18:5 living by doing the statutes) and then shows Matt 7:14's narrow way of conduct leading unto that same life, so that Jesus' claim in John 14:6 is the personification of the already-defined covenant existence. This supplies a uniform, multi-witness symbolic identification that the common eternal-zoe reading does not generate from the same texts without relegating the OT references to a merely temporal domain. Secondary elaborations (tree-of-life-as-nation, highway distinctions, prosphatos reading) are not required for the core and remain open. The counter's strength in wider Johannine formulas is real but does not overturn the supplied evidence or the method's demand for OT-first definitions.
book_core_identification: Covenant existence—the life produced by (walking in) the law/covenant-conduct
book_secondary_elaborations: Tree of life as the living nation/community whose obedience is displayed
Jesus as the Torah embodied (standard + conduct + existence in one person)
Way/truth/life as three inseparable aspects of one Torah reality
Light as the law lived visibly among men
Highway (raised covenant road) distinguished from way (conduct)
strongest_counter_interpretation: In Johannine and broader NT usage 'the life' is the eternal divine life (zoe) that resides in the Son, is given to believers through faith/union with him, and constitutes qualitatively new spiritual existence (present and future) in communion with God, distinct from biological life or merely land/covenant existence under Moses.
counter_core_identification: Eternal/divine life (zoe) embodied in and mediated by Jesus Christ
material_core_denial: Denies that 'the life' is the existence the law itself produces; instead it is the free gift and personal presence of Christ received by faith, while the OT 'live by them' texts refer only to temporal blessing in the land or an unattainable ideal.
counter_case: John 14:6 stands inside a Gospel that repeatedly equates life with eternal life given by believing the Son (John 1:4; 3:16; 5:24-26; 10:10; 11:25; 17:3)
1 John 5:11-12 states explicitly that the life is in the Son and is possessed by having the Son
Deut 30:19-20 and Lev 18:5 function in their original contexts as promises of prolonged physical life and land tenure under the Mosaic covenant, not the eschatological zoe of John
Matt 7:14's 'life' is the end of true discipleship, commonly read as eternal life rather than law-produced covenant status
The definite article and christological 'I am' formulas point to a personal source of life rather than a product of Torah-keeping
book_explanatory_advantages: Supplies a single, OT-derived definition that makes the definite article in John 14:6 intelligible as 'the particular life already defined'
Unifies Deut 30, Lev 18, Matt 7:14 and John 14:6 without splitting the term into temporal vs eternal domains
Explains how Jesus can claim to be 'the life' as the perfect embodiment and walking of the same covenant existence
Integrates 'the life' with the immediately preceding 'way' and 'truth' as one Torah reality now become a person
Follows the book's own multi-witness method (patterns spanning Law, Prophets, Writings) that the parables chapter established as the expected decoding procedure
counter_explanatory_advantages: Accounts for the sheer density of Johannine 'eternal life' / 'life in the Son' language more directly
Preserves the NT emphasis on life as gift rather than product of law-observance
Naturally incorporates the resurrection claim ('I am the resurrection and the life') as power over death
Aligns with the historic consensus across Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant traditions
unresolved_objections: Tension with Pauline assertions that the law cannot give life (Gal 3:21 etc.), which the chapter never engages
Whether 'covenant existence' fully captures the qualitative abundance and resurrection power of Johannine zoe
Secondary claim that the tree of life is the obedient nation requires further symbolic steps not proven solely by the supplied texts
